predicates.title: App registration federated credential with broad OIDC trust and Azure privilege
predicates.description: An app registration has a federated identity credential (OIDC trust to GitHub Actions / Azure DevOps) whose subject is broad (repo-wide, all branches, environment-less, or pull_request) AND the app holds meaningful Azure RBAC. The deterministic trigger (broad subject + privileged role, both runner-projected) is mechanized; exploitability and final severity stay agentic.
predicates.attack_vector: A push or PR in the trusted repository requests an OIDC token and acts as the privileged identity
predicates.recommendation: Constrain FIC subjects to a specific branch/environment/tag; minimize the identity's Azure RBAC; require protected environments for privileged deployments.

predicates.title: User-assigned managed identity federated credential with broad trust
predicates.description: A user-assigned managed identity has a federated credential trusting an external OIDC issuer (GitHub/Azure DevOps) with a broad subject, and the identity holds privileged Azure RBAC. Same escalation path as app-registration FIC but via a UAMI.
predicates.attack_vector: A workflow in the trusted repo obtains a token for the UAMI and exercises its Azure privileges
predicates.recommendation: Pin the federated subject to a specific branch/environment; reduce the UAMI's role assignments to least privilege.

predicates.title: CI/CD-like service principal with broad subscription role
predicates.description: A service principal with a federated credential (a strong CI/CD signal) holds Owner or Contributor at subscription scope or higher. The high-signal FIC-based trigger is mechanized; the fuzzier deployment-style-name inference for non-FIC service principals stays agentic.
predicates.attack_vector: Compromising the pipeline or its trust relationship yields subscription-wide control
predicates.recommendation: Scope CI/CD identities to the specific resource groups they deploy to; avoid Owner; prefer per-environment identities.

predicates.title: Deployment identity still using a long-lived secret instead of federation
predicates.description: A CI/CD-like identity (deployment RBAC and/or an existing federated credential) still authenticates with an active long-lived client secret or certificate rather than OIDC workload identity federation. The static secret is an exfiltration target that bypasses OIDC trust constraints. Metadata only — credential existence/expiry, never the value.
predicates.attack_vector: A leaked pipeline secret authenticates from anywhere, ignoring branch/environment OIDC constraints
predicates.recommendation: Migrate deployment identities to workload identity federation (OIDC) and remove static client secrets.

predicates.title: Container registry admin user enabled or task building from unreviewed source
predicates.description: An Azure Container Registry has the shared admin user enabled (a single static push/pull credential), or an ACR task builds images from a source repository outside the engagement allowlist. The adminUserEnabled trigger is fully deterministic; untrusted-source is runner-projected against the allowlist and labelled 'requires review' when no allowlist is supplied.
predicates.attack_vector: Stolen admin credential pushes a backdoored image; a poisoned source repo or base image is built and deployed
predicates.recommendation: Disable the ACR admin user and use Entra/token auth; restrict tasks to approved source repositories; pin and scan base images.

predicates.title: Automation Account with privileged identity and external triggers
predicates.description: An Automation Account runs with a privileged managed identity (or legacy RunAs) and has enabled webhooks, schedules, or hybrid workers, so triggering a runbook executes privileged actions. Metadata only — runbook source and webhook URLs are not retrieved.
predicates.attack_vector: Invoking a webhook/schedule runs a runbook as the privileged identity, executing attacker-chosen Azure actions
predicates.recommendation: Reduce the automation identity's RBAC to least privilege; restrict/rotate webhooks; review runbook triggers and hybrid worker groups.

predicates.title: Logic App with unauthenticated HTTP trigger or high-risk API connections
predicates.description: A Logic App workflow exposes an HTTP/request trigger without IP restrictions or additional authentication, and/or relies on stored API connections to high-risk connectors. Metadata only — signed callback URLs (listCallbackUrl, a POST) are never enumerated.
predicates.attack_vector: An open HTTP trigger lets an unauthenticated caller drive the workflow and its connected resources
predicates.recommendation: Add trigger IP allow-lists / SAS or AAD auth; review API connections and their connector permissions; restrict who can invoke the workflow.

predicates.title: Plaintext secrets exposed in deployment or automation surfaces
predicates.description: The deployment/automation supply chain exposes secrets in cleartext rather than via Key Vault references — an unencrypted Automation variable (isEncrypted == false), a plaintext deployment parameter that should be secureString/Key Vault reference, or a secret-shaped app/Function setting that is NOT an @Microsoft.KeyVault(...) reference. Metadata only — the presence/shape is flagged, never the value.
predicates.attack_vector: A reader of automation/deployment/app configuration harvests a live credential and reuses it, bypassing identity controls
predicates.recommendation: Store all automation/deployment secrets as encrypted variables or Key Vault references; pass deployment secrets as secureString sourced from Key Vault; rotate any value already exposed.

predicates.title: Container image vulnerability scanning not enforced in the deploy path
predicates.description: Images feeding the pipeline are not subject to enforced vulnerability scanning before deployment — Defender for Containers registry/image scanning is not enabled, no Azure Policy gates vulnerable/unscanned images, and/or ACR quarantine is disabled so unscanned images are immediately pullable. Framed from the supply-chain pipeline angle (push → scan → gate → deploy), distinct from logging's subscription-level Containers plan toggle.
predicates.attack_vector: A vulnerable or backdoored image flows unscanned through the pipeline identity into running workloads
predicates.recommendation: Enable Defender for Containers registry/image scanning, gate deployment on resolved vulnerability findings via Azure Policy, and enable ACR quarantine so only scanned images are pullable.
